title: Bitcoin mining difficulty reaches new all-time high as hash
content:
TL;DR: The Bitcoin network continues its relentless march, operating at block 934,808 with a robust hashrate of 871.38 EH/s. While not at an all-time high, the current difficulty of 146.47 T still secures the hardest money in history, with an imminent adjustment likely to offer temporary relief to miners. Transactors should monitor mempool conditions and prepare for potential fee market shifts as the network recalibrates its security parameters.

The Report

As of February 03, 2026, at 07:01 UTC, the Bitcoin network stands operational at block height 934,808, demonstrating its unwavering commitment to decentralized, censorship-resistant money. The global computational effort securing this ledger, known as the hashrate, currently measures 871.38 Exahashes per second (EH/s). This formidable figure underscores the vast resources dedicated to maintaining Bitcoin's integrity, ensuring transaction finality and protecting the monetary base layer from external interference.

It's crucial to contextualize these numbers accurately. While impressive, the current network hashrate of 871.38 EH/s is below the approximately 977 EH/s (and some readings up to 1042 EH/s) observed in late January 2026. Similarly, the network's mining difficulty, currently at 146.47 T, is robust but notably *not* at an all-time high. The peak difficulty was recorded in November 2025 at 155.9 T. This distinction is vital for transactors, as it shapes mining economics and network dynamics, dispelling any narratives of "record highs" that are not supported by verifiable data.

The network is steadily progressing towards its next difficulty adjustment, a self-regulating mechanism that ensures blocks are found, on average, every ten minutes. We are currently 69.4% through the current difficulty epoch, with 616 blocks remaining until the next recalibration. Given the observed decline in hashrate from late January's ~977 EH/s (which set the current 146.47 T difficulty) to today's 871.38 EH/s, the protocol's algorithm is expected to *decrease* the mining difficulty in the upcoming adjustment. This is a natural and healthy response to fluctuations in mining participation, ensuring the network remains accessible and secure without requiring human intervention.

Globally, the mining sector continues to navigate a complex landscape. Energy prices remain a significant factor, with regional variations impacting miner profitability. Geopolitical stability, or the lack thereof, in key mining jurisdictions can lead to temporary shifts in hashrate distribution. However, Bitcoin's decentralized nature means that no single event or region can cripple the network; miners simply relocate, seeking cheaper energy and more favorable regulatory environments. The ongoing innovation in ASIC technology also drives efficiency, allowing miners to remain competitive even when the difficulty is high, or when energy costs fluctuate.
